properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Indianapolis IN has issued a
Flood Warning for the following rivers in Indiana...

Big Blue River at Carthage.

Clifty Creek at Hartsville.

.Copious rainfall in the past 24 hours, totaling as much as 5 inches
in Bartholomew County and 8 inches in Rush County, are quickly
bringing flooding to the Big Blue River and Clifty Creek today.
Rainfall will taper off the rest of the day, with additional amounts
expected to be under four tenths of an inch.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Big Blue River at Carthage.

* WHEN...From this afternoon until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 11.0 feet, Extensive flooding is in progress. Many
local roads flood and are impassable to most vehicles. A few
evacuations are necessary in southern parts of Carthage, extreme
southern sections of Knightstown, eastern Raysville and a few
rural areas of northwest Rush County. Used auto parts yard in
Carthage is flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 2:30 PM EDT Wednesday the stage was 6.9 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 10.1
feet late tonight.
- Flood stage is 7.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
To escape rising water, take the shortest path to higher ground.

Even 6 inches of fast-moving flood water can knock you off your feet
and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters,
stop, turn around and go another way.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/ind.

The next statement should be issued Thursday morning by around 700
AM EDT.

...The National Weather Service in Indianapolis IN has issued a

.Heavy rainfall of three to well over six inches overnight, and
continued rainfall today and tonight, will bring considerable
flooding to area waterways, including the Mississinewa River.
Significant flooding is expected in the Ridgeville area.

was beginning and currently below flood stage.  The rise is expected
to be rapid today.  Stay weather aware!.

* WHERE...Mississinewa River near Ridgeville.

* WHEN...From this afternoon to late tomorrow morning.

* IMPACTS...At 13.0 feet, Significant flooding of Mississinewa River
in northern Randolph County. Water is likely on SR 1 just south of

and possibly other county roads are flooded. Little League field
in Ridgeville is flooded.  Noticeable agricultural flooding in
progress.

this afternoon to a crest of 12.9 feet this evening. It will
then fall below flood stage late tonight.

- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

To escape rising water, take the shortest path to higher ground.

and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters,
stop, turn around and go another way.

EDT.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued August 12 at 1:13PM AKDT until August 14 at 4:30AM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
Mendenhall Lake gauge levels, along with USGS imagery from Suicide
Basin and water levels within the basin, indicate that the basin is
continuing its release of water into Mendenhall Lake and River.
Levels on the Mendenhall Lake and River will rise through today as
the release continues, with a forecast crest between 16.1 to 16.6
feet expected Thursday morning.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by a glacier-dammed lake outburst is
expected.

* WHERE...The Mendenhall Lake And River near the Mendenhall Glacier
Recreation area, View Drive and below Back Loop bridge.

* WHEN...Until 430 AM AKDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of the area around Mendenhall Lake and along the
Mendenhall River is imminent. Water levels will continue to rise
through today while water temperatures will fall within the lake
and river.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 845 AM AKDT, gauge data reported a glacier-dammed lake
outburst is ongoing. Flooding is expected to begin shortly near
the Mendenhall Lake And River.
- The outburst flood forecast is based on an estimated volume of
water in the glacier dammed lake and an estimated release rate
based on previous events. The extent of water drainage within the
basin (partial or full) can vary widely between outburst flood
events and is a major source of uncertainty in the forecast,
particularly with regard to the peak flood stage.
- For Mendenhall Lake :
At 12:30pm the stage was 6.36 feet and rising.
Flood Stage is 9 feet.
Forecast: A crest between 16.1 and 16.6 feet is expected around
8am and noon Thursday. Water levels will go above minor flood
state around 9:30pm Wednesday. Water levels will go above major
flood stage around 5:45am Thursday.

Impacts:
At 6.7 feet: Nugget Falls trail begins to flood near the "causeway"
at the end of the trail.

At 7.7 feet: Nugget Falls trail begins to flood near the beginning of
the trail. Along the Mendenhall River some sections will experience
bank erosion resulting in dangerous tree fall. These conditions could
make floating the river more hazardous with the higher water levels.

At 9 feet: Water starts to cover Skaters Cabin Road between Skaters
Cabin and West Glacier Trailhead, also water will flow into the
Mendenhall Lake Campground.

At 10 feet: Water levels will inundate Mendenhall Campground with up
to 3 feet of water covering low areas as well as up to 1.5 feet of
water covering Skaters Cabin Road. Portions of West Glacier Trail
will be impassable. Areas along View Dr will start to flood and cause
minor flooding of yards. Closure of pedestrian pathways beneath
Brotherhood Bridge and the trail system on the west side of
Mendenhall River during outburst events.

At 11 feet: Some homes along View Dr will have up to 1.5 feet of
water in yards. Locations below back loop bridge will see bank
erosion along unreinforced river banks along with hazardous
navigation from debris in the river. Homes along the river on Meander
Way will begin to see flooding of some backyards on the outside of
the HESCO levee. Portions of the Dredge Lake Trail System will be
impassable. Flood waters start to reach Dredge Lake.

At 12 feet: Significant bank erosion along unreinforced river banks.
The low section of road past 9374 View Dr will be flooded with up to
0.5 feet of water. Some houses on the south side and the east end of
View Dr will start to flood. Water begins to flood some backyards of
homes on the northside of View Dr as well as other low lying areas.
Back Loop Rd Bridge will be closed during outburst events.

At 13 feet: The low section of road past 9374 View Dr will be flooded
with 2 ft of water. Water begins to flow through some backyards of
homes on the northside of View Dr and flood low lying areas. A few
locations on View Dr will see depths of 1 to 2 feet of water in
homes.

At 14 feet: The low section of road past 9374 View Dr will be
significantly flooded and impassable. Water will begin to flow over
the road from water flowing behind homes on the north side of View
Dr. More homes along View Dr will begin to see moderate to major
flooding. Locations on River Rd with low river banks will begin to
see water approach driveways.

At 15 feet: Major flooding of multiple homes along View Dr. Water
will begin to approach a few homes along River Rd with low river
banks with possible flooding of driveways and 1 to 2 feet of water in
backyards. Up to 1 foot of water covering Riverside Dr at Tournure St
and Mendenhall River School.

At 16 feet: Water starts to overtop the bank and flood low lying
areas near Wildmeadow Ln. Up to 0.5 feet of water will be in the
intersection of Skaters Cabin Rd and Arctic Cir. Some backyards of
homes between Tamarack Ct and Whitewater Ct will start to see flood
waters along with water approaching River Rd near homes with low
river banks and possibly flooding those homes. Water will start to
flood backyards of homes on Meadow Ln and Stikine St.

At 17 feet: This is an estimate that water will be overtopping the
river banks and flooding into the homes around Wildmeadow Ln.
Businesses in the Vintage Park Blvd area will be surrounded and
potentially inundated by flood waters. Homes on Meadow Ln from
Stikine St to Eagle St will be inundated with flood water. Water will
be covering Tournure St from Riverside Dr to Columbia Blvd. Black
Wolf Way and Pond Vista Dr will have water across the roads. All
parts of View Dr will be covered by flood water.
properties.instruction:

television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

The cold water temperatures can increase the threat of hypothermia
and lower the time required to cause hypothermia.
